title: New Tax Regime: Deductions and Exemptions You Can No Longer Claim
description: India's income tax system offers two regimes: the old, with higher rates but many deductions, and the new, with lower rates but fewer deductions. The new regi.

faq.q: ### Is the new tax regime mandatory for everyone?
faq.a: No, the new tax regime is the default option from FY 2023-24, but taxpayers can still choose to opt for the old tax regime if it is more beneficial for them.

faq.q: ### Can I switch between the old and new tax regimes every year?
faq.a: Yes, salaried individuals and those without business income can choose between the old and new regimes each financial year when filing their Income Tax Return.

faq.q: ### What is the main benefit of the new tax regime?
faq.a: The main benefit is lower income tax rates across various slabs and a simplified tax filing process due to the absence of most deductions and exemptions.

faq.q: ### Does the new tax regime impact my employer's contribution to NPS?
faq.a: No, the employer's contribution to your NPS account (up to 10% of Basic+DA, or 14% for central government employees) remains deductible under Section 80CCD(2) even in the new tax regime.

faq.q: ### Is the standard deduction available in the new tax regime?
faq.a: No, the standard deduction of ₹50,000 for salaried individuals and pensioners is not available under the new tax regime.

faq.q: ### What if I have a home loan? Which regime is better?
faq.a: If you have a significant home loan, especially for a self-occupied property where you claim up to ₹2 lakhs interest under Section 24b, the old tax regime is usually more beneficial, as this deduction is not allowed in the new regime.

faq.q: ### Does the new regime affect tax on capital gains?
faq.a: No, the new tax regime primarily impacts tax on income from salary, house property, and other sources. Capital gains taxation rules remain largely unchanged and are independent of the choice between old and new tax regimes.
